layout_dets.text: Abstract—The corrosion behavior of some conventional and high alloy austenitic, ferritic and duplex

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stainless steels has been studied at 50°C in Gulf seawater. The alloys were tested under salt spray conditions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and corrosion rates were determined by applying the electrochemical polarization resistance technique. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting behavior was studied using the potentiodynamic polarization technique. Both exposure and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accelerated tests were employed to study crevice corrosion. The effect of surface finish on crevice attack was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: investigated in detail. Critical crevice solution pH (CCSpH), an important crevice corrosion parameter, was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: determined by a method based on the Oldfield and Sutton mathematical modelling of corrosion in chloride

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: media [J.W. Oldfield and W.H. Sutton, Br. Corros. J. 13, 13 (1978)]. The relationship between pitting

layout_dets.text: potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and pitting resistance equivalent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: presence of alloying elements such as Cr, Mo and N has a significant and beneficial influence on the pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and crevice corrosion resistance of stainless steels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenitic stainless steels have been formidable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: construction materials for marine and offshore structures due to their excellent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion resistance, high strength, easy fabrication and moderate cost. After carbon

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels, austenitic stainless steels AISI 304 and AISI 316 are perhaps the most

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extensively used structural materials for marine installations including desalination

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plants. AISI 316L is a preferred material for marine applications due to its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: outstanding resistance to localized corrosion, however, the greatest shortcoming

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with these types of stainless steel is their vulnerability to pitting and/or crevice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion in the presence of chloride under static or stagnation conditions.1-11 The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: breakdown of the passive film on steel occurs in the presence of chloride ions which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: subsequently results in the initiation of pits. Pitting proceeds by an autocatalytic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: process in which there is a local increase in chloride and acid concentrations due to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion product hydrolysis in cavities.6 The pitting behavior of austenitic steels has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been the subject of numerous studies due to its importance in seawater processing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plants (desalination plants), marine installations and chemical plants.3,12–15 Crevice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion is the direct result of the stagnant solution accumulated within crevices or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: holes on metal surfaces. Crevice corrosion has been quite frequently encountered in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: marine structures, pipelines, pumps and shafts, valves, and at any location where there

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is possibility of water stagnation or deposit formation.15–19 Crevice corrosion attack

layout_dets.text: and 20Cr-6Mo types containing two ranges of nickel: 10–30% and 20-40%. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: following conclusions were drawn from the study regarding resistance to crevice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or polished surfaces; (ii) resistance increases as the temperature decreases from 70 to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance of 316 type steels; and (ii) Ni above 20% did not have any significant effect.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the present work, the influence of dominant alloy additions such as Ni, Cr and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mo on the pitting and crevice corrosion behavior of some conventional and high alloy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenitic, ferritic and duplex steels in Gulf seawater has been investigated. The object

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of this study is to review the role of alloying additions in improving the local corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance of conventional and high alloy stainless steels.

layout_dets.text: DISCUSSION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The salt spray tests, which represent the testing of the materials under severe salt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: environment conditions, carried out on conventional as well as super-austenitic,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: super-ferritic and Duplex steels, show extremely low corrosion rates even after

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exposures of about 5000 h (Table 4). These results indicate virtual immunity of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloys toward salt environments comprising of salt or salt-aerosol atmosphere. In a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: relative sense, the corrosion rates of high alloy stainless steels (SMO 254, 1925 hMo,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Remanit 4575, Monit 44635 and Duplex 2205) are significantly lower than the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conventional austenitic stainless steels (316L and 904L).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The corrosion rate data for stainless steels in seawater indicate that the rates are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: greatly dependent on the composition of the steels particularly on Cr, Mo and Ni

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contents. Considering the pitting resistance equivalent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the various steels

layout_dets.text: studied it has been found that the super stainless steels which customarily have high

layout_dets.text: show lower corrosion rates (Table 5). Similar trends appear to exist between

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Crevice geometry, specific environments and surface conditions are the important

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: factors in determining resistance to crevice corrosion. The greater the magnitude of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parameters like tightness, chloride solution concentration, temperature or surface

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: smoothness, the more severe is the crevice corrosion. The exposure test results of high

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloy stainless steels showed good crevice corrosion resistance. As-received surface

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: samples at

layout_dets.text: solution temperature showed no crevice corrosion for high alloy as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: well as conventional stainless steels within a period of 180 days, which indicates that in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this condition, crevices do not act as sites for corrosion initiation. However, at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: except for 654 SMO, 3127 hMo and Duplex 2205, all other alloys corroded. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maximum depth of attack was in SS 316L. High alloy steel hMo 1925 suffered

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion on five sites but the maximum depth of attack was 0.05 mm with 0.25 CCI.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SS 904L and 254 SMO corroded only superficially.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It was noticed that at

layout_dets.text: 180 grit SiC finished specimens did not corrode to a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: measurable depth of attack except SS 304L, which has a very small yet measurable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crevice corrosion depth. It implies that the conventional stainless steels could resist the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: seawater crevice corrosion under controlled conditions. Under wheel ground surface

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conditions at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: only 304L and 316L gave considerable corrosion depths while the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maximum depth of attack was in 316L but the number of sites attacked in 304L (six)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was more than that in 316L (two) and hence the CCI (CCI = number of site attack ×

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maximum depth of attack) is higher in the case of 304L. This implies that the crevice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion propagation of 304L is higher because of the absence of molybdenum in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloy.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (1) The corrosion rates of conventional austenitic stainless steels and super-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (2) The corrosion rates determined from long duration salt spray tests are about

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: polarization techniques. This has been attributed to the time lag for stabilization of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: protective oxide layer in the two methods.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: relationships with different slopes are observed.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (5) Both conventional austenitic stainless steels as well as super-stainless steels can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be used without risk of corrosion for seawater applications involving crevice/deposit-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: free systems. Besides superstainless steels, conventional stainless steels containing

layout_dets.text: more than 6 Mo% can be used with little risk of corrosion for seawater applications
